PullRequest.Title: Add unified customizations migration page
PullRequest.Body: ## Summary Redesigns the Agent Customizations migration experience around a single **Migrations** entry and a unified migration homepage. - Groups pending migrations by **Your profile** and the active workspace. - Surfaces the existing supported migration flows for prompt files, VS Code user-data agents/instructions, and MCP servers. - Reuses the existing review pages, filtered to the profile or workspace selected from the homepage. - Supports skipping and re-including workspace migrations without changing files. - Provides scoped destination controls for file migrations. Workspace files recommend `.github` destinations, user files recommend `~/.copilot`, and MCP servers retain their fixed workspace-root `.mcp.json` destination. - Returns to the migration homepage after successful migrations and shows a success callout plus persistent, dismissible migration activity with source and destination paths. - Adds responsive dark, light, and high-contrast styling, keyboard/focus handling, Accessibility Help, and an Accessible View. ## UX details - The sidebar exposes one migration count rather than separate migration shortcuts. - Prompt-to-skill migrations are called out as higher risk because prompt-only metadata can be removed. - Completed profile/workspace groups receive a success treatment and no longer show destination controls. - Review-page lists remain virtualized but use simple, always-expanded sections. - Migration activity uses standard disclosure chevrons and remains scrollable within the modal. ## Out of scope This change intentionally does not add Chat Participants guidance, issue creation, agent-assisted verification, or optional multi-root workspace controls. ## Validation - Targeted migration dashboard, editor, configuration, and Agent Host discovery tests - Copilot customization-provider tests and built-in extension compilation - ESLint, CSS stylelint, and whitespace checks - Component fixtures covering overview, review pages, success/activity, skipped/completed states, narrow layouts, light/dark themes, and high contrast

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path from the added line to synchronous geometry reads is direct, and the loop/write ordering is explicit. Exact milliseconds depend on retained history size and browser layout cost, which affects severity but not mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous browser geometry reads and repeated scrollbar layout work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Initial dashboard rendering performs one `scanDomNode()` per persisted activity entry while the DOM is incrementally growing; each scan measures the increasingly large activity tree, so cost grows with history entries and their preceding item nodes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Opening or rerendering the Migrations dashboard can block the UI thread with repeated style/layout calculations and produce visible modal jank for larger activity histories.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no migration activity dashboard and therefore no per-history-entry geometry rescan during page construction.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: For every activity entry, initial rendering calls `updateDisclosure()`, which invokes `onDidChangeContent`; the editor wires that callback directly to `migrationDashboardScrollable.scanDomNode()`. `scanDomNode()` synchronously reads `clientWidth`, `scrollWidth`, `clientHeight`, and `scrollHeight` before rendering proceeds to append more activity content.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added unconditional `updateDisclosure();` executes once for every activity entry during initial rendering and reaches the newly added `onDidChangeContent: () => this.migrationDashboardScrollable?.scanDomNode()` callback.
Findings.Title: Avoid rescanning layout for every activity row during render
Findings.Impact: After multiple migration batches, merely opening or refreshing the dashboard interleaves DOM writes with one forced geometry measurement per entry, instead of measuring once after the complete tree is built. The uncapped persisted history makes the trigger cumulative across sessions.
Findings.Evidence: `renderActivity` calls `updateDisclosure()` at line 288 inside the activity loop. That function always calls `onDidChangeContent`; the editor callback calls `scanDomNode()`, whose implementation reads the element's client and scroll dimensions. Item DOM is appended immediately afterward, ensuring later iterations measure after additional writes. `showOverview` already emits a final content-change callback after rendering, so the per-entry calls are redundant for initialization.
Findings.Recommendation: Initialize `expandedActivity` without notifying during construction, attach the toggle listener, and reserve `onDidChangeContent` for actual user toggles; rely on the existing single callback at the end of `showOverview` to scan after the full DOM is built.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The append-without-limit, profile-scoped persistence, synchronous storage stringify, full-history reads, and full item render loops are directly traced. Only the rate at which individual users accumulate migrations is uncertain, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Persisted JSON bytes, parsed JavaScript activity/item objects, and dashboard DOM nodes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The stored array grows with every successful migration invocation and every migrated item for the lifetime of each profile/harness or workspace/harness key; no count, item, age, or byte limit is applied.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increasing persistent-storage size and progressively higher parse, serialization, allocation, and dashboard-render costs, eventually causing slower migration completion and dashboard opening plus retained memory.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, successful migrations produced notifications and optionally revealed migrated files; they did not retain a persistent per-file activity history or render that history on later visits.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each successful migration now prepends a full entry, including source and destination path strings for every item, to all prior activity and stores the complete object in profile-scoped machine storage indefinitely.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `activity: [entry, ...state.activity]` retains every previous entry whenever a successful migration is recorded; this persistence and activity UI did not exist before the diff.
Findings.Title: Bound the persisted migration activity log
Findings.Impact: A user who performs migrations repeatedly (especially copy migrations whose sources remain eligible, or migrations accumulated over months) grows this record without bound. Every subsequent store synchronously serializes the whole history, while opening the Migrations page parses it and creates item DOM for all entries, including collapsed ones.
Findings.Evidence: `recordMigrationActivity` reads the existing state and stores `activity: [entry, ...state.activity]` with no eviction. `getCustomizationMigrationDashboardOverview` reparses the profile/workspace states and passes all entries to `renderActivity`; that method loops over every entry and every item and allocates the hidden details DOM. The storage implementation stringifies object values on `store`, so both stored bytes and update cost grow with history.
Findings.Recommendation: Apply an explicit retention budget before storing (for example, cap total entries/items or serialized bytes and evict oldest records), and avoid retaining abandoned workspace keys; preserve recent activity and dismissal semantics within that bound.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the customization editor and navigate to the unified Migrations dashboard
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor initialization starts migration discovery; the dashboard cannot show final counts until enabled category computations and destination-folder discovery finish. Once loaded, the dashboard synchronously parses activity state and builds its DOM before it is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt, agent, instruction, and skill files through `listPromptFiles` and read MCP configuration files while creating the migration plan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold discovery is per distinct prompt type, with user/local source enumeration beneath it; MCP configuration reads are grouped by source URI. Warm prompt-file calls reuse `cachedFileLocations` promises.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor already computed enabled migration categories and their candidates before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold discovery gates final migration counts; warm cached prompt discovery reduces this portion, while MCP support/plan resolution can still gate completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for the active agent-host MCP support snapshot and derive migration candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquired support scope for the MCP category per refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same MCP migration computation was already part of migration refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The dashboard remains in its loading state until this completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse profile/workspace activity JSON, sort every retained entry, and construct activity DOM.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: All retained entries for the active profile/harness and workspace/harness, and all items in those entries; history has no bound.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No persistent activity history was parsed or rendered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This synchronous work is on dashboard opening and rerendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled migration categories, distinct prompt types and source folders, MCP config source files, plus total retained activity entries/items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Enabled categories run under `Promise.all`; prompt-type discovery is coalesced by cached promises. Distinct target types are queried concurrently. Refresh sequence checks discard stale results but do not cancel prior work. Dashboard parsing and DOM construction are synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt-file lists use per-type cached promises when locator events support caching; MCP planning is recomputed. Activity state is held as serialized storage values and reparsed on each `getObject`; there is no history cap or negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call paths, cache behavior, synchronous storage parsing, complete-history sorting/rendering, and geometry reads are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical activity histories may initially be small, but the retained history is cumulative and collapsed entries still allocate item DOM. Exact filesystem and agent-host latency varies by provider.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable for unbounded retained activity and repeated synchronous layout scans; discovery boundaries themselves are pre-existing and remain grouped/cached.

Scenarios.Scenario: Migrate selected prompt, agent, instruction, or skill files and return to the dashboard
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After confirmation, target resolution and filesystem migration complete; the new activity record is synchronously assembled and stored. Delete-original migrations then refresh discovery before the success notification and dashboard return.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read each distinct source, choose available target names, create target folders/files or copy/move skill folders, and optionally delete originals.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source read per unique source URI; target existence/name checks and writes scale with migrated customizations; operations execute sequentially by source/customization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same migration function and filesystem operations existed before; the diff only adds source metadata to its result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations are the main migration critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse prior activity and stringify/store the prior history plus the new entry containing every successful source and destination path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One store for each represented profile/workspace context with successful items; bytes processed equal the complete accumulated history for that key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No activity object was persisted after file migration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously after file migration and before the dashboard return.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected files, unique source URIs, target collisions, and cumulative historical migrated items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Filesystem migration is sequential across grouped source URIs and within each source group. Activity mapping is synchronous; no batching or eviction bounds historical serialization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Target names use per-run reserved-name maps. Candidate refresh benefits from prompt-list caches where valid. Activity always reparses and rewrites the complete stored object.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged filesystem behavior and newly introduced unbounded synchronous activity persistence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most users migrate modest file sets, but copy mode can leave sources eligible and future files can create repeated activity indefinitely.
Scenarios.Verdict: The existing filesystem cardinality is unchanged; the new unbounded full-history persistence is reportable.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The service validates the current support snapshot, plans and executes grouped MCP configuration updates, records successful server paths, refreshes candidates, and returns to the dashboard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read source MCP JSON and update source/target MCP configuration files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Planning reads are coalesced by source URI; execution groups candidates by source/target configuration rather than issuing one independent file read per server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: MCP migration already used the same planning and grouped execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Filesystem validation and writes gate migration completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist one activity entry containing all successfully migrated server source/target paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-history rewrite per successful MCP migration batch; entry size scales with migrated servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No MCP activity history was retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous persistence occurs before candidate refresh and dashboard return.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: MCP servers, distinct source/target config files after grouping, and cumulative activity history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: MCP support uses one scope; source reads are memoized per source during planning and execution groups file updates. The new activity store is synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: MCP plans are recomputed against the authoritative support snapshot; no persistent activity cap exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: grouped existing boundary behavior and the new persistence call are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: MCP server counts are usually smaller than file customization counts, but activity accumulation is lifetime-based.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new MCP boundary fan-out; the shared unbounded activity persistence issue applies.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand, dismiss, or revisit migration activity
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening/revisiting synchronously rebuilds all entry and item DOM. Expansion toggles update scroll dimensions; dismissal rewrites the filtered stored state and rerenders the complete dashboard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse complete activity state on render and stringify the remaining complete state on dismissal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: All retained entries/items for reads; all remaining entries/items for each dismissal write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on user interaction and rerender.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Initial activity rendering invokes one measurement per activity entry plus final scans; user toggles require one scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no activity list and no per-entry dashboard scrollbar scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Per-entry measurements are interleaved with DOM writes and can force repeated layout before the page becomes responsive.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total persisted activity entries and the number of item/path nodes preceding each entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All activity DOM creation, geometry measurement, and storage parsing/serialization occur synchronously on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No rendered-row virtualization or lazy item mounting is used; collapsed details retain eagerly created children. Stored JSON is parsed anew on each state read.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the initialization callback directly reaches synchronous dimension reads inside the entry loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Visible jank depends on history size and browser layout cost, but the per-entry forced-measurement pattern and cumulative history are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous layout amplification; initialize disclosure state without per-row notification and scan once after rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Configure scoped migration destinations or invoke Accessible View
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Destination configuration opens one quick pick and optionally one native folder dialog. Accessible View synchronously formats the current checklist and complete activity history only when invoked.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open a native folder picker when the user selects Choose another folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one dialog per explicit destination-selection action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The new dashboard did not expose this scoped custom-destination workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User-requested and expected to gate destination selection, not dashboard loading.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct destination type/storage pairs (bounded by supported prompt types and two scopes) and retained activity items for Accessible View text generation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Quick picks/dialogs are serialized by user interaction; Accessible View formatting is synchronous and on demand.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Selected destinations are held in memory for the active session context and reconciled on refresh; there is no expensive remote cache behavior on this interaction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Accessible View cost inherits activity-history size but is explicitly invoked and secondary to the already reported unbounded retention.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression: the dialog is one user-triggered boundary, and Accessible View scaling is a consequence of the reported history retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 20 changed files. Submitted two findings: unbounded persisted per-item migration activity, and per-entry synchronous scrollbar geometry scans during initial activity rendering. Existing migration discovery, filesystem migration, and MCP planning retain their prior caching/grouping behavior and did not establish additional diff-caused regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
